name: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid
nameAr: إسماعيل بن أبي خالد الأحمسي البجلي الكوفي، مولاهم
fatherName: Abu Khalid (named Sa'd, or Hurmuz, or Kathir)
diedNote: 146 AH (al-Bukhari, from Abu Nu'aym; the Taqrib); Ibn Hibban: 145 or 146.

deathVariants.authority: al-Bukhari, from Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn; Ibn Hajar, Taqrib
deathVariants.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, letter alif, entry 543; Taqrib al-Tahdhib 438

deathVariants.authority: variants listed in the Shamela narrator record

taqrib.ar: ثقة ثبت من الرابعة، مات سنة ست وأربعين
taqrib.en: Reliable, firm; of the fourth generation; died in 146.

role: The most reliable transmitter from al-Sha'bi; junior Successor

teachers.name: Qays ibn Abi Hazim
teachers.source: Sahih al-Bukhari 57; Tahdhib al-Tahdhib: 'and he narrated much from him'

students.name: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah
students.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib ('the two Sufyans'); Sahih al-Bukhari 2157

students.name: al-Hakam ibn Utaybah
students.source: al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, as quoted in Tahdhib al-Tahdhib (the sabiq of the sabiq-and-lahiq pair)

students.name: Ubaydullah ibn Musa
students.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib: 'the last reliable narrator to transmit from him'

students.name: Yahya ibn Hashim al-Simsar
students.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib: 'one of the abandoned narrators, and the last of all to transmit from him' (the lahiq)

verdicts.ar: حفاظ الناس ثلاثة: إسماعيل، وعبد الملك بن أبي سليمان، ويحيى بن سعيد الأنصاري؛ وهو يعني إسماعيل أعلم الناس بالشعبي وأثبتهم فيه
verdicts.en: The memorisers among the people are three: Isma'il, Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman and Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari; and he, Isma'il, is the most knowledgeable of people in al-Sha'bi and the firmest in him.
verdicts.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, letter alif, entry 543; al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 2/174

verdicts.ar: أصح الناس حديثا عن الشعبي ابن أبي خالد
verdicts.en: The soundest of people in hadith from al-Sha'bi is Ibn Abi Khalid.

verdicts.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, letter alif, entry 543; al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 2/174

verdicts.en: Al-Nasa'i described him as one who used the ambiguous formula (tadlis).
verdicts.source: Ibn Hajar, Ta'rif Ahl al-Taqdis (Tabaqat al-Mudallisin), as quoted in the Shamela narrator record; Muhammad ibn Tal'at, Mu'jam al-Mudallisin, entry 11, quoting al-Nasa'i's list

verdicts.en: A Kufan, a Successor, reliable; he was a miller.

verdicts.ar: كان ثبتا في الحديث، وربما أرسل الشيء عن الشعبي، وإذا وقف أخبر، وكان صاحب سنة، وكان حديثه نحو خمسمائة حديث، وكان لا يروي إلا عن ثقة
verdicts.en: He was firm in hadith; he would sometimes transmit a thing from al-Sha'bi without the link, and when pressed he would state it; he was a man of the Sunnah; his hadith were about five hundred; he narrated only from reliable men.

verdicts.ar: لا أقدم عليه أحدا من أصحاب الشعبي، وهو ثقة
verdicts.en: I put none of al-Sha'bi's students ahead of him; he is reliable.
Isma'il used to be called 'the Balance'.

verdicts.ar: مرسلات ابن أبي خالد ليست بشيء
verdicts.en: The unattached (mursal) reports of Ibn Abi Khalid are nothing.

verdicts.ar: كان إذا حدث عن قيس يقول: حدثني قيس بن أبي حازم
verdicts.en: When he narrated from Qays he would say: 'Qays ibn Abi Hazim narrated to me.'

verdicts.ar: حدث عنه الحكم بن عتيبة ويحيى بن هاشم، وبين وفاتيهما نحو من مائة وعشر سنين
verdicts.en: Al-Hakam ibn Utaybah and Yahya ibn Hashim both narrated from him, and between their deaths lie about one hundred and ten years.

tadlis.type: tadlis al-isnad, as described by al-Nasa'i; al-Ijli says he would sometimes drop the link from al-Sha'bi
tadlis.source: Ibn Hajar, Ta'rif Ahl al-Taqdis bi-Maratib al-Mawsufin bi-l-Tadlis (Tabaqat al-Mudallisin), second rank, as quoted at shamela.ws/narrator/644 ('the reliable, the famous, among the junior Successors; al-Nasa'i described him with tadlis') and as placed in the Mulakhkhas of the Tabaqat under 'those whose tadlis the imams tolerated' (usul.ai)
tadlis.note: The rank is taken from the Mulakhkhas summary and the Shamela quotation; Ibn Hajar's own page (Ta'rif Ahl al-Taqdis p. 99, ed. al-Qaryuti) was not read directly. In Bukhari 57 the question does not arise: Isma'il says 'Qays ibn Abi Hazim narrated to me', the formula Yahya al-Qattan says he always used for Qays.

notHeardFrom.name: Anas ibn Malik
notHeardFrom.authority: Ali ibn al-Madini: 'he saw Anas, a sighting, and did not hear from him'

flags.label: Sabiq and lahiq
flags.detail: Al-Khatib notes that two of his students, al-Hakam ibn Utaybah and Yahya ibn Hashim al-Simsar, died about one hundred and ten years apart; Ibn Hajar adds that Yahya ibn Hashim, an abandoned narrator, was the last of all to transmit from him, and Ubaydullah ibn Musa the last reliable one. A long teaching life is one of the things the discipline records about a narrator because it bears on who could plausibly have heard from him.

flags.label: Mursal reports not relied on
flags.detail: Yahya al-Qattan dismissed his unattached reports, and al-Ijli says he would sometimes narrate from al-Sha'bi without stating the link. His connected reports from al-Sha'bi and Qays are, by contrast, the soundest there are (Ahmad, al-Thawri, Abu Hatim).

bio: A Kufan client of Ahmas of Bajilah, among the junior Successors; he met several Companions and narrated from five of them, and was the most knowledgeable and firmest of all narrators from al-Sha'bi, and narrated abundantly from Qays ibn Abi Hazim. Sufyan al-Thawri counted him one of the three memorisers of the age and his contemporaries called him 'the Balance'. Al-Nasa'i noted that he sometimes used the ambiguous formula; the imams tolerated it because he transmitted only from reliable men, and from Qays he habitually said 'narrated to me'. He died in 146.
